decisions.decision: How should weekly ML work be coordinated?
decisions.context: The weekly run must be repeatable, while new model ideas should reach production quickly. A three-person team needs a workflow that limits manual coordination.
decisions.rationale: The chosen workflow supports a safe weekly run and fast iterations. “MLOps: Continuous delivery and automation pipelines in machine learning” and “Productionizing Machine Learning with a Microservices Architecture” describe repeatable stages; the design point supports this direction, though it warns that data ingestion must be decided first.
consequences: Pipeline stages and dependencies need ownership.
Data ingestion design remains to be settled.

decisions.decision: How should past forecasts and training runs be reproduced?
decisions.context: The system must reproduce forecasts for any past week, which requires retaining the model and the inputs and configuration used to produce each result.
decisions.rationale: This choice covers dataset versions, pipeline definitions, artifacts, runs, and deployment status needed to reproduce a past week. “MLOps Principles” and “Continuous Intelligence: Moving Machine Learning Application into Production Reliably” support lifecycle traceability; the checked design point selected this value, while a simpler artifact-versioning rival offered less coverage.
consequences: Record dataset and code versions for each run.
Persist run parameters and output metadata.
Maintain a traceable model promotion history.

decisions.context: Demand is forecast weekly per store and product, with no stated requirement for request-time predictions. A scheduled scoring run can produce results for downstream use.
decisions.rationale: The weekly cadence supports scheduled batch scoring and the brief gives no low-latency requirement. “Three Levels of ML Software” and “Architecting a Machine Learning Pipeline: How to build scalable Machine Learning systems - Part 2/2” describe batch prediction delivery; the checked point selected this option, though it also flags the unresolved ingestion decision.
consequences: Publish a dated forecast set after each successful run.
Define handling for late or failed runs.

decisions.decision: How should code and model changes reach production?
decisions.context: New model ideas should reach production quickly without breaking the weekly forecast run. Release automation can validate changes before promotion.

alternatives.label: Recovery-oriented release automation with manual intervention

decisions.rationale: Automated builds, tests, and staged promotion let the team iterate while guarding the weekly run. “MLOps: Continuous delivery and automation pipelines in machine learning” and “Continuous Intelligence: Moving Machine Learning Application into Production Reliably” support this release path.
consequences: Keep the prior production model available for recovery.
Maintain automated build and release workflows.

decisions.decision: How should production forecasts be monitored?
decisions.context: A weekly forecast can degrade as inputs or demand patterns change. The system needs visibility to detect problems before relying on a faulty forecast set.
decisions.rationale: Input and feature checks can flag a changed weekly data profile and prompt investigation before forecast use. “Productionizing Machine Learning with a Microservices Architecture” and “MLOps Principles” support monitoring changes in features; drift alone does not establish forecast accuracy, so quality evaluation remains an uncovered design detail.
consequences: Define expected input schemas and profiles.
Investigate drift before changing the production model.
Add forecast quality checks when labels become available.

uncovered: Data ingestion mechanism and source-of-truth selection; the workflow coordination dimension explicitly requires this decision first.
Forecast evaluation metrics, acceptance thresholds, and model promotion criteria.
Historical raw data retention and point-in-time reconstruction policy for each past week.
Forecast consumer interface, access control, and delivery format.
Infrastructure and scheduling platform appropriate to the team's operational capacity.
